questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle unattended, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is injured.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. If possible, move it off the road. Check for injuries and call 911 if needed. Call the police if anyone is hurt, someone dies, or there is more than $1,000 in damage.

questions.question: Texting while driving is:

options.text: Always legal, but not recommended.
Illegal.
A safe activity.
Legal if you use voice-to-text technology.

questions.explanation: In Washington State, texting while driving is against the law. It is a dangerous distraction and can result in a ticket.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than daytime driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat faster at night.
You cannot see as well in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:

options.text: Loss of concentration.
Poor coordination.
Slower judgment.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road narrows ahead.
There are several curves ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road has three or more curves coming up.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if it is different from the guard's instructions.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the regular traffic rules as if no children were present.

questions.explanation: Follow the directions of any crossing guard, sign, or officer in a school zone. Always drive carefully in school zones.

questions.question: Signaling before you turn, change lanes, or leave a curb:

options.text: Is only necessary if other cars are near.
Is a good habit and is required by law.
Is only needed during the maneuver, not before.
Is not needed if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good habit and is required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal your intentions well in advance before changing lanes or turning. By law, you must signal at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle right or left. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop right away.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people, but try to stop any serious bleeding by applying pressure. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. This helps other drivers know what you are doing and prevents accidents.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
You must turn left ahead.
Do not enter.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Look at what other cars around you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. You should:

options.text: Stop where you are right now.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, slow down and safely pull to the right side of the road. Stop to let the emergency vehicle pass. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly to the side as soon as you can.

questions.question: If you drive a vehicle registered in Washington State, you must:

options.text: Have liability insurance and carry an ID card showing you have it.
Carry insurance only if you ride a motorcycle or drive a large truck.
Carry insurance only if you are under 18 years old.
Carry insurance only if your car is less than five years old.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have liability insurance and carry an ID card showing you have it.
questions.explanation: All drivers in Washington State must have liability insurance and carry proof of it.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and drive past the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to scare them so they do not cross against the light again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross safely, even if you have a green light. Be careful around pedestrians at all times.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:

options.text: Make turning harder.
Increase the risk of hydroplaning.
Increase your stopping distance.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires make turning harder, increase your stopping distance, and raise the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Using a hand-held cell phone to make a call while driving:

options.text: Is safer than using a hands-free phone.
Is allowed only for teenage drivers.
Is illegal.
Is recommended.

questions.explanation: In Washington State, it is against the law to use a hand-held cell phone while driving. If you need to call someone, stop your vehicle safely first.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Leave more space between your car and the car ahead.
Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You cannot see as well at night. Take steps to stay safe and protect other drivers.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: A minor safety problem.
A serious safety problem.
Safe if you only drink a little.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while drinking or using drugs is a serious safety problem. It is dangerous to you and everyone on the road.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and very dangerous. You may turn right on red if no sign says you cannot.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer to escort you back to your exit.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next exit. Never stop, back up, or cross the median on a highway. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
One-way traffic.
Limited parking.
Playground ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead. Watch for trains and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them to retaliate.
Show them you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between your car and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: On a freeway, you miss your turn or exit. What should you do?

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane.
Stop and back up.
Continue to the next exit or safe place where you can turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to the next exit or safe place where you can turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, go to the next safe place to turn around. Never back up on a freeway or shoulder. It is illegal.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving compared to other factors?

options.text: The same way alcohol does.
The same way amphetamines do.
The same way anger does.
The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.explanation: Fatigue harms your driving ability the same way alcohol does. Being awake for 18 hours impairs you like having a 0.05 percent blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours straight impairs you like having a 0.10 percent blood alcohol level.
